decisions.quote:
Our analysis, while applying a different metric from
           Daoust et al. (2022), uncovers a subtler but still significant trend of linguistic under-
           representation in Canadian political science syllabi. While Daoust et al. reported a
           stark absence of francophone scholars in core course materials, our study confirms
           and quantifies this gap while suggesting a significant, though less extreme, under-
           representation.
decisions.reason: The study is a completed replication that collects two new datasets (2022 Canadian politics course syllabi and faculty/Google Scholar records) to re-test and extend Daoust, Gagnon, and Galipeau (2022). In the Discussion, the authors state an explicit overall replication verdict that their study 'confirms and quantifies this gap' of francophone under-representation reported by Daoust et al. (2022), though with a less extreme magnitude once baselines are introduced. Under the codebook's Rule 1 and definition of 'successful', an explicit authorial confirmation governs even when the estimated effect is smaller or varied across baseline assumptions.
